description:
Problem: the patch-hash carry (_project/scripts/oracle_reviewers/protocol.py:124-211,383-461) normalises per-file hunks, function headings and occurrence counts to reuse a prior decision across rebases. In the 2026-10-24..26 window it carried 4.4% of reviews and needed two fix PRs (#3420 headingless and relocated hunks, #3354 retarget). Binary patches hash the abbreviated 10-hex index line, so about 2^40 work forges a carried SHIP onto a different binary. Open item oracle-hunk-headingless-and-repeated-heading-collisions-20261024 tracks a remaining relocated-hunk SHIP hole.

Outcome (owner Q12): a decision carries only when the merge-base-to-head diff is byte-identical to the reviewed one, computed with full blob ids (files API sha, or git --full-index locally), including mode changes, renames and binary files; anything else gets a fresh review. Delete the normalisation code that becomes dead.

Decision gates:
1. The digest covers, per file, old path, new path, old mode, new mode, merge-base blob id and head blob id (full ids): in CI from the files API plus the merge-base git tree, locally from git diff --raw --full-index against the merge base; carry nothing if any field is missing (for example a truncated file list).
2. Base-change and retarget invalidation (#3354) keep working; existing retarget tests stay green.
3. One digest for everything (owner 2026-10-26): this digest also keys strikes, forced or dispute rounds and maintain counts. A rebase onto a develop that changed the same files gives a new digest, which can add a strike and resets the per-patch round allowance; pin these effects with tests and document them.
4. Re-read #3540 (604856dd7), which changed protocol.file_patches and the local digest, before editing.
